commits.messageBody:
proxy.maxBloomFilterSize capped the SBBF body at 32 MiB, which admits about
24.3M int64 members at the default fpr. Raise it to 64 MiB and lift
proxy.grpc.serverMaxRecvSize from 64 MiB to 128 MiB so the larger blob has room
alongside the rest of the request.

This makes 50M members *expressible*; it does not make them work at the default
fpr. A 64 MiB body holds ~48.6M members at fpr=0.005, and 50M at that rate wants
65.77 MiB of bits, which the power-of-two round-up takes to a 128 MiB body. The
smallest fpr that keeps 50M inside 64 MiB is ~0.0058 ((1-e^(-n/B))^8); fpr=0.01
holds ~55.4M. Callers at this scale must raise the fpr explicitly.

The old error reported byte counts only, which leaves "send fewer members" as
the apparent remedy when the real fix is one step of fpr. The over-size error
now reads the declared member count from the MBF1 header and reports the
smallest fpr that would fit, derived by inverting the SBBF sizing formula at the
usable budget:

  bloom_match filter blob body is 134217728 bytes, exceeding
  proxy.maxBloomFilterSize (67108864); rebuild the filter with fpr >= 0.0058
  for the declared 50000000 members (SBBF bodies are powers of two, so a
  smaller fpr jumps straight to the next size)

The hint runs before envelope validation, so n_declared is read defensively and
only decorates an error that was already decided; a malformed blob cannot turn
it into a wrong verdict.

Tests cover that rebuilding at the suggested fpr actually fits across member
counts straddling the boundary, that the bound is tight rather than merely
sufficient (0.0058 fits, 0.0057 does not), that 50M at the default fpr really
does need 128 MiB, that malformed headers and absurd member counts degrade to
no hint instead of panicking, and that a count too large for any accepted fpr
says so instead of suggesting one.

The limit is 64 MiB rather than a value with headroom above it. The gate is
`len(blob) > maxSize + mbf1HeaderSize`, so a full 64 MiB body plus its header
passes exactly, and since SBBF bodies are powers of two every value in
[64 MiB, 128 MiB) admits the same set of filters. A larger number would only
imply capacity that does not exist.

Nothing else in the chain moves: proxy.maxBloomFilterPlanSize stays at 128 MiB,
which still admits one 64 MiB blob plus its plan wrapper, and
proxy.grpc.clientMaxSendSize / queryNode.grpc.serverMaxRecvSize stay at 256 MiB.
Note the aggregate plan budget now fits only one filter of this size: two 64 MiB
bloom_match leaves, or two hybrid sub-searches each carrying one, exceed it.
Raising that budget is a separate, deliberate decision.

Raising the proxy receive limit doubles the largest request an unauthenticated
caller can make the proxy buffer. A blob of size B costs roughly (3 + shards) x B
in transient proxy memory per query and is fanned out to every shard, so filters
at this scale suit low-frequency analytical queries; rate-limit them via
quotaAndLimits rather than treating the new ceiling as an online budget.

Documentation that quoted the old defaults is updated with it: the sbbf and
client API comments, the C++ prober's comment, and the design doc's capacity
tiers and resource-protection section.

Verified: planparserv2, pkg/util/paramtable and client/v3 suites pass,
golangci-lint reports no issues, and configs/milvus.yaml matches the paramtable
value and Doc string byte for byte. internal/proxy tests were not run locally
(they link segcore, which is not built in this tree); nothing here touches that
package.
